title: caboose-coalescence-weekly-sketch-2026-03-21
content:
Weekly sketch: Caboose Coalescence (kernel + KV cache + batching)

Date: 2026-03-21 standup / sync.
Owners in room: Aisha (notes), Lucas (kernel lead), Ben (cache), Rina (perf), Mateo (oncall).

Top-line summary:
- Small wins on steady-state throughput: the coalescer flow cut token CPU by ~8% in our 2k-concurrent synthetic load. p95 latency improved from ~72ms to ~61ms in the happy-path bench (50-token avg).
- Regression observed under cold-start scenarios: tail latencies spike on first two requests after worker spin-up when coalescer sampling warms up.
- KV cache eviction tuning (LFU->windowed-LRU hybrid) shows promise to reduce cross-slice misses but introduced a sequencing edge with prefetch hooks that can reorder requests in very specific timing windows.

What we tried this week (short notes):
- Kernel patch: 'coalescer-bucket-merging-v2' (PR 1473) moved merge logic off hot path and introduced a lightweight header for batch targets. Bench results: steady-state CPU down 8%, GPU occupancy unchanged. Risk: additional memcpy for small-batch cases.
- Cache policy experiment: windowed-LRU (WLRU) with 5-second hot window. Reduced miss rate on chatty sessions by 14% in traces from staging customers.
- Batching heuristic tweak: prefer bounded microbatching for sequences <32 tokens. Lowered p50 by 20% for small prompts but increased p99 by ~3% in bursty arrival tests.

Incidents / Blockers:
- Cold-start tail: observed 3x spike on p99 during worker spin-up. Hypothesis: initial coalescer sampler state is empty so first few requests are serialized into single small batches plus extra KV misses. Action: add warm-up stub requests during startup and prefill basic sampler distribution. Owner: Ben. ETA: 2026-03-25 for patch.
- Reordering edge from cache prefetch: race when prefetch fetch completes after batch commit, occasionally reintroducing older KV pages into the active window which invalidates expected token offsets. This surfaced in integration test suite (test-kv-replay-07). Workaround: serializing prefetch commit to kernel idempotent path. Owner: Lucas. Status: hotfix in review.

Metrics snapshot (staging canary, 2026-03-20):
- Synthetic 2k concurrent, 50-token prompts:
  - p50: 18ms -> 14ms (post-patch)
  - p95: 72ms -> 61ms
  - p99: 220ms -> 205ms (noisy)
  - Throughput units/sec: +12% steady
- Real trace (prod-like): KV miss rate down 14% for active sessions, cold-session miss rate unchanged.

Decisions reached:
- Merge coalescer-bucket-merging-v2 to canary cluster behind feature flag; monitor for memcpy regressions on small-batch tails. (Lucas + Rina)
- Roll WLRU into canary only for sessions with >3 requests in 60s window; conservative rollout to avoid evict thrashing. (Ben)
- Deprioritize aggressive microbatching for <32 tokens until we can address burst p99 increase; revert if p99 > baseline during canary. (Aisha)

Open questions / notes to self:
- Is memcpy overhead worse on smaller GPUs (T4-ish) vs A100? We need a cross-hardware microbenchmark. (Rina to run)
- Should sampler warm-up be synthetic or replay real recent trace samples? Synthetic is simpler but may misrepresent distribution. (Discussion item next sync)
- How to expose coalescer diagnostics in Console? We should add a small per-route metric: 'coalescer-buckets-per-second' + histogram of batch sizes. (product + console ticket)

Action items and owners:
- Ben: implement startup warm-up stub and measurement harness; target 2026-03-25.
- Lucas: finish prefetch-commit serialization hotfix and push PR for review; ETA 2026-03-23.
- Rina: run memcpy microbench across GPU types and report variance; ETA 2026-03-27.
- Mateo: add alert for cold-start p99 spike (threshold: 2x baseline for 5m) and add to oncall runbook. ETA 2026-03-24.
- Aisha: prepare short canary checklist and metric dashboards for the week-1 rollout. ETA 2026-03-23.

Experiment logs (brief):
- exp/2026-03-18-coalesce-v2: steady-state CPU -8%. Notes: disable in small-batch-only tests due to memcpy noise.
- exp/2026-03-19-wlru-window-5s: KV miss -14% on long sessions. Notes: needs conservative rollout.
- exp/2026-03-20-microbatch-bound-32: p50 win but p99 regressions in bursty arrivals.

Meeting artifacts to link (tickets/PRs): ENG-1987 (coalescer followups), PR#1473 (coalesce merging), test-kv-replay-07 failing trace attached in CI, slack threads: #serving-runtime > March 20 discussion.

Retro-style notes (informal):
- Wins: team shipped a non-trivial refactor without destabilizing the runtime; good coordination across kernel/cache/ops.
- Friction: too many late-night debug sessions for rare prefetch race; need earlier integration-test coverage for prefetch ordering.
- Idea: add a small deterministic simulator that can fuzz prefetch ordering and batch merge timings — cheap to run in CI. Would catch the subtle reorder case and speed up turnaround.

Next sync: short 20m deep-dive Tuesday 2026-03-24 10:00 PT; focus: cold-start warm-up plan + canary metrics checklist.

Notes to self (scratchpad):
- remember to add 'coalescer-debug=true' flag to staging route for richer telemetry (token-level traces).
- follow up with product on console metric naming so dashboards are consistent with rollout checklist.
- final thought: if windowed-LRU reduces cross-slice thrash, consider exposing window size as heuristics per-customer (dedicated customers may prefer larger window).

End of sketch.
